vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/self-referential-mapping-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-20: the anchored mapping `a` contains an alias to itself, so its expansion is unbounded. The code is the D-18 code, document.limit.alias-expansion, at `$` (D-18, D-22). No declared limit is carried: an unbounded W exceeds every finite maximum, so the vector needs no configuration surface and every implementation runs it. A reader that materializes a cyclic structure, or loops, has failed D-20 whatever it reports.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/self-merge-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-20, the self-merging form: `a` merges itself. Before omnist#352 the reference accepted this and materialized `{k: 1}`; D-20 says it is unbounded and MUST be rejected, not resolved by dropping the cycle.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/self-referential-sequence-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-20 for a sequence anchor: `a` is a sequence whose only member is an alias to `a`.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/cycle-through-two-anchors-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-20 for a cycle "through other definitions": `a` contains `b`, and `b` refers back to `a`. Neither definition refers to itself directly.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/self-referential-root-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-20 where the cyclic anchor is the document root, which is a candidate node like any other (D-18).

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/redefined-anchor-referring-to-itself-is-a-cycle
vectors.comment: D-27 with D-20: an alias inside the definition that carries its own name refers to that definition, not to the earlier `&x`, so `b` is self-referential. The new definition shadows the earlier one from the point where it begins, including inside itself.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/alias-to-undefined-anchor-is-a-syntax-error
vectors.comment: D-27: no definition of `x` exists, so the alias refers to nothing. YAML makes this an error, and the code for input that is not well formed in its source format is parse.codec-syntax (the position is the E-32 placeholder).

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/alias-before-its-anchor-is-a-syntax-error
vectors.comment: D-27: an anchor defines a name only for the aliases that follow it. `x` is defined, but after the alias, so this is the same error as an undefined anchor.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/redefined-anchor-scalar-later-alias-uses-latest
vectors.comment: D-27: redefining an anchor is legal, not an error (YAML 1.1 and 1.2 both say an alias refers to the most recent preceding definition of the name). `c` reads 2.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/redefined-anchor-mapping-each-alias-uses-nearest-preceding
vectors.comment: D-27: the alias before the redefinition (`b`) keeps the first `&x`; the alias after it (`d`) takes the second. A reader that applies one definition to the whole document, first or last, fails one of the two.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/quoted-merge-key-is-an-ordinary-key
vectors.comment: D-27: only a plain `<<` is a merge key. A double-quoted `"<<"` is the string `<<` and makes an ordinary edge labelled `<<` holding the aliased mapping; `q` is NOT `{x: 1}`. (The explicitly tagged forms are not decided by D-27.)

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/quoted-merge-key-with-a-scalar-value-is-not-malformed
vectors.comment: D-27 against D-18a: a plain `<<: 1` is a syntax error (a merge value must be a mapping or a sequence of mappings), but a quoted `"<<"` is not a merge key at all, so the scalar value is fine.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/aliases-inside-a-tagged-omap-count-toward-expanded-size
vectors.comment: D-27 (a tag does not change what an alias contributes) with D-22. W(p) = 11. The tagged sequence t holds two single-entry mappings, each an alias to p: W(t) = 1 + 2 * (1 + 11) = 25 and W(root) = 1 + 11 + 25 = 37. Counted as scalars instead (the defect D-27 rules out), the two aliases would be one slot each and W(root) would be 1 + 11 + 5 = 17. The declared maximum of 20 sits between the two, so only a reader that skips the items of a tagged collection accepts this input. No expansion factor is near its limit (E(t) = 25 / 5 = 5.00 against 50), so the vector isolates the expanded size. declared_max_expanded_slots is vector-local; an implementation with no configuration surface reports skip, not fail. What Document shape the tagged collection produces is not decided, and the vector does not depend on it.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/single-quoted-merge-key-is-an-ordinary-key
vectors.comment: D-27: the single-quoted `'<<'` is the string `<<`, like the double-quoted form.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/merge-key-uses-the-nearest-preceding-definition
vectors.comment: D-27 in merge position: `b` merges the first `&x`, `d` the second.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/undefined-alias-in-merge-position-is-a-syntax-error
vectors.comment: D-27: the undefined-alias rule holds where the alias is a merge value too.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/undefined-alias-in-a-flow-sequence-is-a-syntax-error
vectors.comment: D-27: and inside a flow sequence.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/anchors/undefined-alias-wins-over-a-limit-code
vectors.comment: D-27: an undefined alias is malformed input, so it is reported as parse.codec-syntax even though `t` alone would exceed the declared expansion maximum of 2 (E(t) = 6.50, as in the D-18 worked example); the same precedence D-18a states for a malformed merge. The undefined alias comes after the bomb.
